The upstream outputs answer this only partially: the module inventory (`modules`) covers the whole repo, but the three other tasks each cover a small corner of it. `entrypoints` returned symbols only from the Python `camon` package and its tests, `functional-surface` profiled only the `site` module, and `module-tree` returned two modules and one edge.

From the inventory, the repo is a multi-part monorepo: a main `src/` tree (agent providers, analyze, cli, config, daemon, db, docgen, indexer, mcp, shared, workflow) with a mirrored `out/` tree, two IDE plugins (`jetbrains-plugin`, `vscode-plugin`), a Python package `camon`, and a small `site/js` front end. The only part whose behaviour is grounded in symbols is `camon`: a mitmproxy-addon-based monitor that records AI-agent traffic usage (provider, agent, token usage), stores it, and exposes it through a CLI, a TUI, reports and exports.

How the parts connect is largely unanswered. The only graph-derived edge is `camon/tests` → `camon/src/camon` (16 imports). No dependency edges, entrypoints or exports were returned for `src/`, `out/`, the plugins or `site`, so any statement about how the main backend, the plugins and `camon` relate would be ungrounded and is omitted.

findings.title: Repo layout: main `src/` tree, mirrored `out/` tree, two IDE plugins, a Python package and a site
findings.detail:
Per `modules`, the repo `/Users/subhagho/work/projects/insors/insrc` contains these module families:

- **`src/`** — the main tree, with `src/agent/providers`, `src/analyze` (classifier, context, executor, explore, orchestrator, planner + templates, runtimes for code/data/docs/generic/infra/shared, summariser), `src/cli` (hooks, panes, services, ui), `src/config`, `src/daemon` (artifacts, db + drivers + converters, tools + builtins), `src/db` (graph, lance), `src/docgen` (extract, render), `src/indexer` (parser, target-resolution), `src/mcp`, `src/shared`, `src/types`, `src/workflow`, `src/bin`, `src/assets/docgen`.
- **`out/`** — a tree whose directories mirror `src/` (e.g. `out/analyze/explore`, `out/daemon/tools/builtins/git`, `out/workflow/runners/build`). It contains no `__tests__` directories, and lacks some newer `src/` areas such as `docgen`, `workflow/code-review`, `workflow/review`, `workflow/bugfix` and `mcp/review-step`.
- **`jetbrains-plugin`** — sources under `src/main/kotlin/ai/insors/insrc/jetbrains` (actions, daemon, debug, freshness, host, lifecycle, onboarding, ops, platform, review, settings, steering, ui, workflow) with a matching `src/test/kotlin` tree, plus `build/` outputs.
- **`vscode-plugin`** — `vscode-plugin/src` (chat, config, daemon, delivery, freshness, hosts, models, onboarding, panels, surfaces, workspace), `vscode-plugin/out`, and indexed third-party code under `vscode-plugin/node_modules/esbuild` and `vscode-plugin/node_modules/marked`.
- **`camon`** — `camon/src/camon` (15 files) and `camon/tests` (9 files).
- **`site/js`** (1 file), **`tmp/pdfs`** (1 file) and the repo root (2 files).

The inventory gives directories and file counts only; it carries no purpose descriptions, so what each `src/` area does is inferred from its name alone.

findings.title: `src/daemon/tools/builtins` is a broad set of tool groups
findings.detail: Per `modules`, `src/daemon/tools/builtins` has one subdirectory per group: `cloud` (`aws` 14 files, `az` 10, `gcp` 11), `code` (with `migration` and `orm`), `data`, `db`, `docs`, `file` (11), `gh` (8), `git` (24), `graph`, `http`, `k8s`, `notify`, `pkg`, `search` (5), `shell` (6), `ssh`, `test`, `web`. `git` is the largest group. No symbols from these directories were returned, so their individual behaviour is not described.

findings.title: `src/mcp` and `src/workflow` are organised as per-step and per-runner modules
findings.detail:
Per `modules`:

- `src/mcp` has step-style subdirectories: `analyze-step` (+ `phases`), `build-step` (+ `phases`), `code-review-step`, `deploy-step`, `review-step` (+ `phases`), `triage-step` (+ `phases`), `workflow-step` (+ `phases`), plus `docgen`, `guide`, `schema`.
- `src/workflow` has `amendments`, `artifacts` (companion, format, provenance), `bugfix`, `code-review` (+ `dimensions`, with `diagram/handlers` and `ux`), `config`, `delivery`, `locate`, `review`, `tracker`, `triage`, and `runners` for `brainstorm`, `build`, `define`, `design-epic`, `design-story`, `issue`, `plan`, `stub`, `tracker`.
- Test weight is concentrated in `src/workflow/__tests__` (56 files), `src/analyze/context/__tests__` (42), `src/daemon/__tests__` (34) and `src/mcp/__tests__` (21).

The parallel naming suggests each `src/mcp/*-step` module fronts a `src/workflow` area, but no import or call edge in the upstream confirms it.

findings.title: `camon`: a mitmproxy-addon monitor for AI-agent traffic and token usage
findings.detail:
Per `entrypoints`, all returned symbols are in `camon/src/camon` and `camon/tests`. By file:

- `addon_runtime.py` — classes `CamonAddon` and `AddonStorage`; helpers `_provider(host)`, `_agent(user_agent)`, `_usage(content)`, `_default_database_path()`, `_retention_days()`.
- `extract.py` — `provider_for_host`, `usage_from_json`, `estimate_tokens`, `safe_url_parts`.
- `attribution.py` — `classify_text(text, rules)` and class `ProcessAttributor`.
- `models.py` — `Attribution`, `UsageEvent`, `AddonStatus`.
- `config.py` — `AppConfig`, `AgentRule`, `default_data_dir`.
- `storage.py` — class `Storage`.
- `registration.py` — `register_local_addon`, `_register_macos`, `_register_linux`, `_update_macos_program_arguments`, `addon_path`, `addon_mitmdump`, `addon_database`.
- `runtime.py` — `ProxyState`, `detect_mitmproxy`, `restart_managed`, `_known_service_pid`.
- `setup.py` — `AgentSetup`, `detect_agents(proxy_url)`, `setup_agent(...)`, `_write_claude_settings`, `_claude_settings_configured`, `launcher_path`, `mitmproxy_ca_cert_path`.
- `reporting.py` — `render_report(storage, days)` and `export(storage, target, format, days)` with format `json` or `csv`.
- `tui.py` — class `CamonApp` plus formatting helpers (`_sparkline`, `_format_token_count`, `_format_bytes`, `_format_uptime`).
- `cli.py` — `main` (with a `--background-color` option) and commands `status`, `register`, `restart`, `report`, `export`.

Test names in `camon/tests` describe the intended behaviour: recording a completed flow without mutating it, writing and rotating per-agent traffic logs, extracting usage without persisting the body, purging data outside a retention window, recording request/session/daily usage, rejecting a non-local agent at registration, rejecting restart of an unmanaged proxy, creating an opt-in proxy launcher, and merging proxy environment into Claude settings.

findings.title: Connections inside `camon`, as far as signatures show them
findings.detail:
No call graph was returned for `camon`; these links are read from signatures in `entrypoints` only:

- `cli._services()` returns `tuple[AppConfig, Storage]`, so the CLI depends on `config.py` and `storage.py`.
- `reporting.render_report` and `reporting.export` both take a `Storage`; the CLI has `report` and `export` commands with matching `days` (and `format`) parameters.
- `runtime.restart_managed(config: AppConfig)` takes the config type; the CLI has a `restart` command.
- `attribution.classify_text` takes `Iterable[AgentRule]`, tying attribution to `config.py`.
- `registration.register_local_addon(retention_days)` fans out to `_register_macos` / `_register_linux`, which share the `(addon, retention_days)` shape; the CLI has a `register` command.
- `addon_runtime.py` carries its own `AddonStorage` class and its own `_provider` / `_usage` helpers alongside `Storage` in `storage.py` and `provider_for_host` / `usage_from_json` in `extract.py`. Whether the addon reuses or duplicates those is not determinable from the upstream.

The one graph-derived edge, per `module-tree`, is `camon/tests` → `camon/src/camon` via 16 imports.

findings.title: `site`: one browser script of page-behaviour initialisers, no exports
findings.detail: Per `functional-surface`, the `site` module has an empty `exports` list and 17 internal helpers, all in `site/js/tui.js`. They are initialisers and their nested helpers: `initTheme` (with `currentTheme`, `paintToggle`), `initNav`, `initNavOverflow` (with `closeMenu`, `openMenu`, `layout`, `bar`, `schedule`), `initCopy` (with `done`), `initAnchors`, `initType`, `initTabs` (with `select`, `fromHash`). `modules` lists `site/js` with a single file. Nothing in the upstream links `site` to any other module.

findings.title: Gap: entrypoints cover only `camon`, not the main `src/` tree or the plugins
findings.detail: `entrypoints` returned symbols from `camon/src/camon` and `camon/tests` only. Many are private helpers (`_integer`, `_format_bytes`, `_backup`) and test functions, so the list reads as a symbol dump of one package and not a set of real entrypoints. No entrypoint was returned for `src/bin`, `src/daemon`, `src/mcp`, `src/cli`, `jetbrains-plugin` or `vscode-plugin`. What the main backend and the plugins actually do is therefore not grounded in any symbol in this run.

findings.title: Gap: the dependency graph has one edge, so cross-module connections are unanswered
findings.detail: `module-tree` returned two modules (`camon/src/camon`, `camon/tests`) and one edge between them, against several hundred modules in `modules`. There are no edges among `src/` modules, none between `src/` and `out/`, and none from `jetbrains-plugin`, `vscode-plugin`, `camon` or `site` to the main tree. The second half of the focus question (how the parts are connected) cannot be answered beyond `camon`'s own test-to-source edge. A rerun scoped to `src/` would be needed for the main backend's topology.

findings.title: Gap: functional surface was profiled for `site` only
findings.detail: `functional-surface` profiled a single module, `site`, and found no exports. No public surface was returned for any `src/` module, either plugin, or `camon`, so the exported API of the main code is not described here.

findings.title: Inventory includes build output and vendored code
findings.detail: Per `modules`, the indexed set includes non-source directories: the whole `out/` tree, `vscode-plugin/out`, `jetbrains-plugin/build/reports/tests/test/js`, `jetbrains-plugin/build/resources/main/insrc-review`, `vscode-plugin/node_modules/esbuild` (+ `lib`), `vscode-plugin/node_modules/marked` (`bin`, `lib`, `src`) and `tmp/pdfs`. Module and file counts for the repo are inflated by these, and they should be excluded when reading the inventory as a picture of authored code.
